description: Brief notifications that slide up from the bottom of the screen, stack, and dismiss on a timer or with a swipe.
overview:
`Toaster` wraps your app in a toast provider and renders the queue through a portal into a full-screen viewport. On iOS the viewport sits inside a `FullWindowOverlay` from `react-native-screens`, so toasts appear above native modals. Each toast is a Reanimated view that slides in from the bottom edge, fades out downward, and is capped at 384 points wide.

Visible toasts stack with a small peek and shrink behind the frontmost one. Touching the stack expands it; it collapses again three seconds after the touch ends. Each toast shows an icon for its `type` (`success`, `info`, `warning`, `error`, or a spinner for `loading`), a title, a description, an optional action button and a close button.
usage:
Render `Toaster` once near the root, then call the exported `toast` manager from anywhere: `toast.add({ title, description, type })` returns an id, `toast.update(id, updates)` changes a toast, and `toast.close(id)` removes it (or all toasts when called without an id).

`toast.promise(promise, { loading, success, error })` shows a loading toast and replaces it with the success or error state when the promise settles.

Pass `actionProps` (for example `{ children: "Undo", onPress }`) to show an action button. Set `priority: "high"` for urgent messages and `timeout` to override the provider default; `loading` toasts stay until updated.

Use `createToastManager` to create a separate manager and pass it to `Toaster` as `toastManager`, and `useToastManager` to read the current toasts and actions inside the provider. The lower-level parts are exported for building a custom toast layout.

examples.ShowOnLoad: Shows a success toast as soon as the screen mounts.

parts.Toaster: Provider, portal and viewport that render the default toast list.
parts.ToastProvider: Holds the toast queue, default timeout and visible limit.
parts.ToastPortal: Renders its children into a portal host.
parts.ToastViewport: Full-screen layer that holds the stack and expands it on touch.
parts.Toast: One animated, swipeable toast in the stack.
parts.ToastContent: Row layout for the icon, text, action and close button.
parts.ToastTitle: The toast title, read from the toast object.
parts.ToastClose: Icon button that dismisses the toast.

Toaster.toastManager: Manager whose toasts are shown. Defaults to the exported `toast`.
Toaster.timeout: Default auto-dismiss time in milliseconds. Defaults to `5000`.
Toaster.limit: Maximum number of visible toasts. Defaults to `3`.
Toaster.portalHost: Name of the portal host to render into.

Toast.swipeDirection: Direction or directions that dismiss the toast with a swipe. Defaults to `down` and `right`.

accessibility:
- Each toast has the `alert` role and a live region that is `polite`, or `assertive` for `priority: "high"`.
- New toasts are announced with their title and description; high-priority announcements are not queued.
- A `dismiss` accessibility action and the escape gesture close the toast.
- Toasts stacked behind the front one are hidden from VoiceOver and TalkBack.
- The close button has the label "Close toast" and the type icon is hidden from assistive technology.
- Animations respect the system reduce motion setting.
notes:
- Uses `bg-surface-raised`, `text-label`, `text-label-secondary` and tint tokens `bg-green`, `bg-accent`, `bg-orange` and `bg-danger` for the icons.
- Light and dark colors follow the system appearance; dark mode drops the border.
- Toasts respect the bottom safe area inset.
- `FullWindowOverlay` is used on iOS only; Android renders the viewport directly.
